items.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Feasting With $120M+ in Franchise’s Box Office Comeback
items.summary:
Lionsgate's "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" opened in 4,018 North American theaters and took in $56 million on Friday, including Thursday previews, putting the sixth film in the franchise on course for a weekend north of $120 million. That Friday number ranks fourth in series history, ahead of 2015's "Mockingjay — Part 2" ($45.6 million) and 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" ($19 million), and behind "Catching Fire" ($70.9 million), the 2012 original ($67.2 million) and "Mockingjay — Part 1" ($55.1 million).

The Hollywood Reporter noted that Lionsgate had publicly projected an opening above $80 million, while other tracking put the figure between $100 million and $130 million. Francis Lawrence directed the roughly $150 million adaptation of Suzanne Collins' prequel novel, which is set 24 years before the events of her 2008 book. Joseph Zada plays a young Haymitch Abernathy, the role Woody Harrelson originated, with Ralph Fiennes as President Snow and a supporting cast that includes Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak and Maya Hawke.

The result reverses the franchise's downward slide. "Songbirds & Snakes," starring Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer, opened to $44 million and finished with $166.4 million domestically and $361.8 million worldwide, the series' weakest entry and its only B+ CinemaScore. "Sunrise" drew an A- from opening-weekend audiences, a 67 percent critics score on Rotten Tomatoes and a franchise-best 95 percent audience score.

By the end of the weekend the series total should sit near $3.437 billion, making "The Hunger Games" Lionsgate's biggest franchise ever, past "The Twilight Saga." The opening also ranks fifth in studio history and fifth among 2026 domestic debuts, and it stands as the largest launch of the careers of Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning. The release landed a day after "Grand Theft Auto 6" arrived, with no visible drag.

Elsewhere, Amazon MGM widened Peter Farrelly's "I Play Rocky" to 2,477 theaters for an estimated $9.3 million and a rare A+ CinemaScore, the year's second. Paramount's "Ebenezer," Ti West's Dickens reimagining with Johnny Depp, should take third with about $8.2 million and a $33 million cume, while Warner Bros.' "The Cat in the Hat" adds roughly $7 million for $47.2 million. Focus opened Simon Stone's "Elsinore," with Andrew Scott, in six theaters for about $240,000.

items.title: Princess Of Wales Documentary ‘Heal’ Set At BBC & NBC; Special About Kate Middleton’s Cancer Journey Gets Release Date & Trailer
items.summary:
The Princess of Wales is the subject of a documentary called "Heal," which the BBC will air in the UK on November 29 and NBC will carry in the U.S. on November 30. The film follows Catherine as she takes on the National Three Peaks Challenge and talks about her life after a cancer diagnosis. It is the first documentary she has headlined.

The challenge itself took place in June, when she climbed the highest peaks in Scotland, England and Wales inside 24 hours in support of The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. As Deadline reported, a crew filmed the climb for the documentary, and the project's existence had been kept quiet until now. All proceeds from the film's distribution go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.

Built around the climb, "Heal" has Catherine speaking with others who have faced serious illness about what a diagnosis does to a patient and to the people around them, and about the places and experiences that help during recovery. The trailer includes her brother James, who joined her for one of the climbs, and closes with Prince William and their children, George, Charlotte and Louis, meeting her at the finish.

Detail Films produced the documentary and Benji Jackson directed. In the U.S., NBC runs it at 8 p.m. on November 30, with a Bravo airing at 11:30 p.m. the same night and a Peacock release the following day. The BBC broadcast is set for 6:15 p.m. GMT on November 29.

NBCUniversal has also set international dates, with Channel 9 in Australia carrying it on December 1 and CTV in Canada on December 7. Prince William has fronted documentaries before, including "Prince William: We Can End Homelessness," and he and Prince Harry made "Diana, Our Mother: Her Life and Legacy" nearly a decade ago. Harry and Meghan Markle have produced several docuseries under their Netflix deal, among them "Harry & Meghan."

items.title: CAA’s Bryan Lourd Urges Congress to Pass NO FAKES Act to Combat AI Deepfakes: ‘Every One of Us Should Have the Right to Say No’
items.summary:
CAA chief executive Bryan Lourd called on Congress to pass the NO FAKES Act in a New York Times opinion piece published Saturday, arguing for a federal rule governing unauthorized AI likenesses. "Every one of us should have the right to say no to an unwelcome use of our likeness," he wrote.

The bill, reintroduced by Sen. Chris Coons in May after an earlier attempt last year, cleared the Senate Judiciary Committee in June with bipartisan co-sponsors but has not reached a floor vote. Lourd wrote that it would establish a national standard built on "control, consent and compensation," replacing what he called "outdated, ill-fitting state laws, many of them written with an analog world in mind."

Lourd framed his argument around his day job rather than policy expertise. "I run a global talent agency. Part of our job is to help our clients license their likenesses and performances, sometimes to AI companies," he wrote, adding that CAA negotiates those deals regularly and that the pending bill "delivers what the industry needs and what will protect all Americans."

Variety reported that he pointed to Tom Hanks, who alerted his followers in 2023 that a dental practice had used an AI-generated younger version of him in an advertisement. Lourd's point was not that Hanks would have signed off, but that he was never asked. "What's missing is a bright-line rule affirming that right in the AI age, and it is one Congress can supply before the year is out," he wrote.

CAA has been active on the issue outside of Washington, working with the Human Consent Foundation, backed by Cate Blanchett, on tools that let people set permissions for their likenesses when AI models scrape them. The agency also joined the foundation and other entertainment groups on an amicus brief in the New York Times case against OpenAI, citing the licensing market for likenesses that has formed since 2022.

Support for the NO FAKES Act spans an unusual range of parties, including SAG-AFTRA, the Motion Picture Association, the RIAA, the Recording Academy, the National Association of Broadcasters, the AFL-CIO, YouTube, IBM and OpenAI. The measure remains with the full Senate.
